newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close one percent lower on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: French shares close one percent lower on Thursday.

text.p: French shares closed one percent lower on Thursday on profit-taking from recent record highs on the last day of the July Bourse account, dealers said.

A lower Wall Street and a 1.6 percent drop in Frankfurt also weighed on prices. But dealers said that as long as the dollar remained at its current levels, posting a year high against the franc today, the share market fall would remain limited.
The CAC-40 index closed down 30 points, or one percent, at 2,973.53. The CAC-40 July futures ended 41 points lower at 2,979.
The broader SBF120 index was down 16.63 points at 2,028.8
Volume was 12.3 billion francs of which 8.9 billion in CAC-40 stocks.
Carmaker Peugeot was the biggest riser with a 5.19 percent gain to 648 francs with the stock catching up with Renault's recent advances.
Sidel made a 5.06 percent gain at 456.50 francs. It had been suspended on Wednesday when it announced a share bid for Gebo.

Usinor was the biggest volume stock, adding 4.50 francs to 125 in a turnover of 1.3 billion francs. It closed earlier at 1430 GMT today because it will join the CAC-40 index on Friday, replacing Suez which merged with Lyonnaise des Eaux, down 0.85 percent at 698 francs.
Biggest faller was L'Oreal, down 3.7 percent at 2,453 francs in thin volume.
